results.title: Informative Priors: Bayesian Statistics Essentials
results.content: Informative priors are a crucial component of Bayesian statistics, allowing researchers to incorporate prior knowledge into their models. * **Informative priors**: These are prior distributions that incorporate prior knowledge or information about the parameter. Prior elicitation is the process of determining the prior distribution based on prior knowledge or information. flowchart LR A["Define problem and parameter"] --> B["Elicit prior distribution"] B --> C["Specify prior distribution"] C --> D["Update prior with data"] D --> E["Analyze results"] E --> F["Validate results"] F --> G["Refine prior or model"]. The mathematical representation of informative priors involves specifying a prior distribution for the parameter of interest. By understanding the fundamentals of informative priors, eliciting and specifying prior distributions, and implementing them in practice, researchers can make more accurate predictions and better decisions. ### What are informative priors in Bayesian statistics? ### How are informative priors elicited? Some common challenges when working with informative priors include prior-data conflict, prior elicitation bias, and model misspecification.
